equations.objective: J(V) = lambda*||V-W||_F^2 + erase*||V X^T - W G^T||_F^2 + preserve*||V R^T - W R^T||_F^2, X,G,R arranged tokens-by-input-dimension ([77,768]); V,W are [d_out,768] per-layer projection weights (to_v or to_k).
equations.normal_matrices: H = lambda*I_768 + erase*(X^T X) + preserve*(R^T R)  [768x768, independent of layer, depends only on the cell's X and the fixed R]; N_layer = lambda*W_layer + erase*(W_layer (G^T X)) + preserve*(W_layer (R^T R))  [d_out x 768, per layer]
equations.stationarity_condition: V*_layer . H = N_layer  (V* = N_layer @ H^-1, valid since H is symmetric)
equations.derivation_check_performed: dJ/dV = 2*lambda*(V-W) + 2*erase*(V X^T - W G^T) X + 2*preserve*(V R^T - W R^T) R, set to 0, algebraically reduces to V.H=N above -- confirmed by hand before coding, cross-checked against edit_model_adversarial's own mat1/mat2 accumulation (mat2 -> H, mat1 -> N, projection_matrices[layer_num].weight = mat1 @ inverse(mat2) -> V = N @ H^-1).
equations.why_each_layer_uses_its_own_pre_edit_W_d: The 32 layers are 32 DISJOINT weight matrices (16 to_v + 16 to_k of different cross-attention modules). The outer `for layer_num in range(32)` loop reads `projection_matrices[layer_num].weight` into mat1/mat2 and only overwrites that SAME layer_num's weight at the end of its own iteration; no other layer's update touches it. So each layer's target is built from that layer's own weight as it stood when this edit_model_adversarial call began, regardless of traversal order -- not because of any ordering safeguard, but because distinct layers never alias the same tensor. (Note this is layer-independence WITHIN one call; the row-level W we audit, B_UCE.pt/AB_UCE.pt, is itself the pre-edit weight supplied to the Stage-2 call we are auditing -- the question of how THAT weight was produced by Stage 1 is out of scope here.)
equations.quadratic_gap_identity: J(V) - J(V*) = tr( (V-V*) H (V-V*)^T )  [derived by hand from the bilinear expansion of J; H symmetric, N=V*H], checked numerically against the direct objective difference with tolerance 1e-8*max(1,|J(V)|,|J(V*)|).

numerical_method.upcast: All operands (W, X, G, R, V_native) cast to float64 BEFORE forming H and N -- not by casting an already-rounded float32 Gram matrix.
numerical_method.solve: H V*^T = N^T solved per-layer via Cholesky factorization of H (symmetric; expected positive-definite since lambda=0.1>0 adds a strictly-positive diagonal floor to a PSD sum of Gram matrices). No explicit matrix inversion. H (and its Cholesky factor) depends only on the cell's X and the fixed R, so it is identical across all 32 layers within a cell and is factored ONCE per cell and reused for all 32 layers (4 factorizations total, not 128).
numerical_method.fallback_if_cholesky_fails: If Cholesky fails (not PD within fp64 tolerance), this is reported as an unresolved reference-validity diagnostic (per task section 5), not patched with jitter, truncated SVD, or altered regularization.
numerical_method.threads_and_devices: torch.set_num_threads bounded to a small fixed count; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' set in the audit process environment; no .cuda() call anywhere in the script; no CUDA allocation at any point.
numerical_method.memory: Each of the 6 required UNet checkpoints (~3.4GB fp32 each) is loaded once, the 32 needed cross-attn to_k/to_v tensors are extracted and upcast, and the full state dict is freed before moving to the next checkpoint.

metrics_per_layer_per_cell: H: finite (all elements), symmetry error ||H-H^T||_F, min/max eigenvalue, spectral condition number (lambda_max/lambda_min)
Normalized stationarity/backward error for native V and reference V*: ||V H - N||_F / (||V||_F * ||H||_2 + ||N||_F)  [||H||_2 = lambda_max, H symmetric PSD]
||V_native - V*||_F relative to ||V*||_F, and relative to native edit displacement ||V_native - W||_F
J components (regularization/erase/preserve) and total J, evaluated at V=W, V=V_native, V=V*
Absolute excess objective J(V_native)-J(V*), and relative excess (J(V_native)-J(V*)) / max(1e-30, |J(V*)|)
Quadratic gap tr((V_native-V*) H (V_native-V*)^T), compared against the direct objective difference J(V_native)-J(V*)
Output-rounding comparison: V*_fp32 = V*.to(fp32), then J evaluated at V*_fp32.to(fp64) -- isolates output-rounding scale only, not all native computation error

Zero-denominator handling: any ratio whose denominator underflows below 1e-30 is reported as the raw numerator/denominator pair with the ratio marked undefined, never silently dropped or clamped to a nonzero floor without saying so
aggregation: Per-layer tables (32 rows) published per cell, not just an average.

Per-cell aggregates: total J over all 32 layers for W/V_native/V*, total quadratic-norm quantities (sqrt of summed squared Frobenius norms across layers) for displacement/backward-error numerators, and median + maximum per-layer relative error (both the normalized backward error and ||V-V*||_F/||V*||_F) -- max reported explicitly so a single bad layer cannot hide in an average.

validation_tolerances_frozen_before_inte.reference_backward_error_tolerance: normalized backward error for V* must be <= 1e-10, per layer, or that layer's reference solve is reported as an unresolved diagnostic, not interpreted.
validation_tolerances_frozen_before_inte.quadratic_gap_identity_tolerance: |[J(V_native)-J(V*)] - tr((V_native-V*)H(V_native-V*)^T)| <= 1e-8 * max(1, |J(V_native)|, |J(V*)|); cancellation in this check is reported where the two terms are large and close.
validation_tolerances_frozen_before_inte.note: These tolerances validate the fp64 reference solve's OWN internal consistency. They are not image-quality or research-success thresholds, and are not relaxed after seeing results.

decision_rule_frozen_before_interpretati: Native outputs differ materially from V* (excess objective beyond simple float32-output-rounding scale, per layer or in aggregate) -> numerical implementation becomes a concrete candidate mechanism for the embedding_cross_swap quality differences, requiring a separately authorized image-level follow-up to test (not run here).

Native outputs closely match V* -> this specific erase-solver numerical-accuracy explanation is closed; any large erase/retain residual in J is then interpreted as a constraint-tradeoff property of the (lambda, erase, preserve) weighting itself, not a solver defect. No precision tuning is performed in response.

Mixed or provenance-limited evidence (e.g. a missing/mismatched input, a failed Cholesky, a reference backward-error or identity-check tolerance violation) -> reported as an explicit unresolved diagnostic for the affected cell/layer, with aggregates for that cell marked provisional; not papered over by excluding the failing layer from the average.
Agreement between native and V* does not by itself validate the embedding-recovery step (close_form_emb_regzero) that produced E_D/E_S -- that is a different computation, not tested by this audit.
max_scope: One CPU-only linear-algebra audit script, run once per cell (4 cells x 32 layers = 128 layer-cell audits).
No golf-subspace search, no norm scaling, no alternative reference construction, no new concept, no stable-solve image generation, no automatic follow-up.
No replacement model checkpoint is assembled from any diagnostic per-layer solution.
